runs.title: Sen. Chris Murphy's stroke: what's the latest?
runs.prompt: Connecticut US Senator Chris Murphy suffered a stroke earlier this week and, per his office, will not return to the Senate next week. Today (Friday, November 6, 2026) he was reportedly discharged from hospital. Find out the latest: was he discharged, is he going to rehab, and what has the Senator or his office said in their own words? Report the details and name the source of any official statement. Start with his official Senate press room and news outlets; avoid paywalled sources.
runs.answer: Yes — Sen. Chris Murphy was discharged from The Johns Hopkins Hospital on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, and he said he will spend the next several weeks in a rehabilitation center, missing several weeks of Senate votes while staying engaged remotely. He disclosed he suffered a small bleed in the thalamus region of his brain; Dr. Jose Suarez, chief of neurosciences critical care at Johns Hopkins, confirmed a small hemorrhagic stroke and said "He has shown tremendous progress, and at the current rate of improvement, we expect that he will make a full recovery following rehabilitation." In his own words: "Last Saturday afternoon, I felt something was not right with my body and called 9-1-1 out of an abundance of caution, and I'm glad I did"; "This has been a scary experience for me and my family, and I appreciate the continued respect for our privacy"; "I want to extend my deepest thanks to the excellent doctors and staff at Johns Hopkins who have treated me and cared for my family." The statement is the Senator's own, reported via his office; the earliest account (numbness in his arm at his son's hockey game, transfer to Johns Hopkins) came from an earlier statement by his chief of staff. runs.title: Blackwood nursery rat closure: the facts
runs.prompt: A children's nursery in Blackwood, South Wales — Greenfields Nursery — has been permanently closed following reports of a rat infestation, and two people have reportedly been arrested on suspicion of child neglect. Find out (respectfully and factually): why it was closed, who runs it, what the regulator or police have said, and where parents can find official information. Avoid unverified social-media claims; prefer local news and official statements.
runs.answer: Care Inspectorate Wales (CIW) took enforcement action to suspend the registration of Greenfields Day Nursery in Blackwood on 20 October 2026 — a temporary step taken while it investigated concerns — and the setting has since closed permanently after reports of a rat infestation; CIW says its priority is children's safety and wellbeing and that it is working with partner agencies. The nursery is run by managing director Jason Robert-Jones, who disputes the rat account (describing a minor rodent issue) and insists the decision to close permanently was his, not CIW's. Gwent Police arrested two people on suspicion of child neglect — a 49-year-old man from Cardiff and a 29-year-old woman from the Caerphilly area — after Caerphilly County Borough Council referred concerns to police on 3 November; both were later released on conditional bail while enquiries continue, and the council says it is supporting affected families. Parents seeking official information or alternative childcare should contact Caerphilly's Family Information Service (the route CIW itself points families to) and check CIW's register for the setting's registration status, rather than relying on social media.

runs.title: Jett Cleary to Penrith: the deal details
runs.prompt: NRL halfback Jett Cleary, brother of Nathan Cleary, has reportedly signed to return to the Penrith Panthers, reuniting the brothers. Find out the specifics: how long is the deal, what have the Panthers officially announced (their own news release), and what does it mean for Nathan Cleary's future at the club? runs.answer: Jett Cleary, 21, has signed a two-year deal to return to Penrith, his junior club, after being granted a release from the Warriors, where he spent the past two seasons and made his NRL debut. Penrith confirmed the signing on Friday 6 November 2026; the club's own release quotes football manager Shane Elford: "We're excited to have Jett return to the club. He's a talented young halfback who came through our pathways, and it's been pleasing to see him continue his development and earn his NRL debut. He returns with valuable experience and a strong connection to Panthers. We look forward to seeing him build on that progress and take the next step in his career here." It points to Nathan staying: days earlier his management told the PNG Chiefs he was staying put, and he is working towards a four-year extension (final two years in his favour) taking him to 2031 at about $1.7m a season — well short of the Chiefs' $2m tax-free offer — while he recovers from tightrope ankle surgery and targets round one.
